acceptance_criteria.criterion: listAllProjects() returns projects from two stores with correct store_id and store_label fields on each project
detectProjectByCwd() returns MULTI_STORE_AMBIGUOUS with tagged candidates when the same cwd matches projects in different stores
getMergedRegistry() returns entries with store-order priority — the first store's entry for a duplicate repo name is returned, the second store's is suppressed
getRegistryConflicts() correctly identifies repos registered in multiple stores and designates the winner by store-order priority; returns empty when no overlaps exist
searchKnowledge() returns merged results from all stores, deduplicated by insight id (first-seen wins)

Adding a new store directory (with its own .repositories.json and projects) to the StoreRouter immediately makes its repositories and projects visible via listAllProjects() and getMergedRegistry() without any additional registration step

summary: Implemented MultiStoreManager class in mcp-server/src/storage/multi-store-manager.ts providing cross-store read operations: listAllProjects() (with store_id/store_label/store_path tagging), detectProjectByCwd() (with MULTI_STORE_AMBIGUOUS for cross-store collisions), getMergedRegistry() (store-order priority, tagged entries), getRegistryConflicts() (winner by store order), searchKnowledge() and listKnowledge() (dedup by numeric insight id, first-seen wins).
Extended StoreRouter with label? on StoreRef and the new getAllStores() method that returns [{id, path, label}] — used by MultiStoreManager internally to iterate stores with metadata.

Created three test suites: multi-store-manager.test.ts (listing/detection AC 1–2), multi-store-conflicts.test.ts (registry AC 3–4), cross-device-portability.test.ts (knowledge dedup AC 5, portability AC 6). All 24 new tests pass; full suite of 3755 tests passes with zero regressions.

comments.note: StoreRouter.getAllStores() returns store metadata used by MultiStoreManager, but the StoreRef internal interface now carries label? even though it was not previously needed. A minor refactor to keep label only in getAllStores() (reading from config directly) would reduce the internal surface, but the current approach is clean enough for this stage.

KnowledgeStoreManager.searchInsights() applies pagination (limit/offset) per store before cross-store merge in MultiStoreManager.searchKnowledge(). Passing limit/offset to per-store calls truncates results before dedup, so the final merged list may return fewer items than the requested limit when dedup removes duplicates. A future improvement could collect all results then apply pagination — but that changes the semantics agreed to in WP-004 scope, so it is noted here for QA awareness.

Both stores independently start their next_id counter at 1, creating structural id collisions across stores (insight id=1 in store-1 and insight id=1 in store-2 are different insights). The dedup-by-id rule suppresses the second store's entry. This is documented and tested, but the test fixture in cross-device-portability.test.ts 'returns results from both stores' had to add a 'Duplicate placeholder' insight to bump store-2's counter past the collision. A future scoped-id scheme (e.g. prefixed by store) would eliminate this ambiguity entirely.

One medium edge-case gap identified in detectProjectByCwd(): FOUND in store-1 is silently discarded when store-2 returns AMBIGUOUS, contradicting the JSDoc comment. No AC covers this scenario; flagged for future hardening.

comments.note: detectProjectByCwd() — FOUND + AMBIGUOUS mixed result: When store-1 returns FOUND (foundProjects.length===1) and store-2 returns AMBIGUOUS (intraStoreAmbiguous!==null), the guard `foundProjects.length===1 && intraStoreAmbiguous===null` fails, and the code falls through to return the store-2 AMBIGUOUS — silently discarding the valid store-1 FOUND. The JSDoc documents the intended behaviour as 'Intra-store AMBIGUOUS (no FOUND in any store): forward as-is' but the implementation does not enforce the 'no FOUND' guard. No test covers this path. Requires a data state where two projects in the same store share the same project root (already a data-integrity problem), so practical exposure is low. Recommend adding a guard: if foundProjects.length === 1 return FOUND unconditionally, and document that intra-store AMBIGUOUS is only forwarded when foundProjects is empty.

The 'forwards intra-store AMBIGUOUS' test only asserts `result.status !== 'MULTI_STORE_AMBIGUOUS'` — it accepts both FOUND and AMBIGUOUS as valid outcomes. Adding an explicit `expect(result.status).toBe('AMBIGUOUS')` assertion would make the test more precise and would also immediately catch the FOUND+AMBIGUOUS edge case above.

Pagination pre-truncation in searchKnowledge()/listKnowledge(): limit/offset options are forwarded to each per-store call before the cross-store merge, so the caller may receive fewer than `limit` items when dedup removes cross-store duplicates. Documented by Developer and accepted as out-of-WP-004 scope. Should be addressed in a follow-on work package if the GUI surfaces knowledge views with paginated cursors.

One Blocking logic bug found in detectProjectByCwd(): the guard `foundProjects.length === 1 && intraStoreAmbiguous === null` silently discards a valid store-1 FOUND when any store returns an intra-store AMBIGUOUS — contradicting the JSDoc which states FOUND must win unconditionally. Fix: remove `&& intraStoreAmbiguous === null` from the guard condition.

comments.note: BLOCKING — detectProjectByCwd() guard bug in multi-store-manager.ts (line ~157): `if (foundProjects.length === 1 && intraStoreAmbiguous === null)` must be changed to `if (foundProjects.length === 1)`. The extra `&& intraStoreAmbiguous === null` condition means that when store-1 returns FOUND and store-2 returns an intra-store AMBIGUOUS, the code falls through to `return intraStoreAmbiguous` — silently discarding the valid FOUND. The JSDoc explicitly states the contract: 'Intra-store AMBIGUOUS (no FOUND in any store): forward as-is.' The fix is one character: remove `&& intraStoreAmbiguous === null`. After the fix, add a test: seed store-1 with one project (projectRoot A), seed store-2 with two projects sharing the same projectRoot A (to produce intra-store AMBIGUOUS in store-2), call detectProjectByCwd(A), and assert result.status === 'FOUND'.

[documentation-forward] detectProjectByCwd() FOUND branch returns `{ status: 'FOUND', meta: foundProjects[0]! }` where foundProjects[0] is a TaggedProjectMeta (with store_id, store_label, store_path on the runtime object). The JSDoc says 'The meta does not carry store tags' — this is correct from the declared type perspective (DetectProjectResult.meta is typed as ProjectMeta) but could mislead consumers who inspect the runtime shape. Add a clarifying sentence: the runtime object is a TaggedProjectMeta but callers should rely only on the ProjectMeta shape via the declared type.

[documentation-forward] The 'forwards intra-store AMBIGUOUS' test in multi-store-manager.test.ts uses `expect(result.status).not.toBe('MULTI_STORE_AMBIGUOUS')` — intentionally loose because LedgerStore.detectProjectByCwd may return FOUND or AMBIGUOUS depending on the gap-threshold logic. Add a comment in the test explaining why the assertion is loose, so future contributors don't tighten it without understanding the underlying ambiguity.

Pre-pagination semantics in searchKnowledge()/listKnowledge(): limit/offset are forwarded to each per-store KnowledgeStoreManager call before the cross-store dedup merge, so the caller may receive fewer items than `limit` when dedup removes cross-store duplicates. This is the same debt already documented by the Developer and QA. Acknowledged as deferred — worth tracking in a follow-on WP before the GUI surfaces paginated cross-store knowledge views.

comments.note: multi-store-manager.ts detectProjectByCwd(): the original guard `foundProjects.length === 1 && intraStoreAmbiguous === null` was logically incorrect — the intraStoreAmbiguous sentinel is orthogonal to whether a definitive FOUND exists. The fix `foundProjects.length === 1` matches the JSDoc contract ('Intra-store AMBIGUOUS (no FOUND in any store): forward as-is') because the AMBIGUOUS forward path is now only reached when foundProjects is empty. The scenario that triggered the bug (two projects in the same store sharing the same projectRoot) is itself a data-integrity anomaly, so real-world exposure was low, but the code contract is now correctly enforced regardless of store state.
No other code smells observed in the files touched during rework. The MultiStoreManager implementation remains clean and consistent with surrounding patterns.
